Rashi on Pesachim 59a:10:1.hebrew: ומחוסר כפורים - כגון מצורע או זב ששכח ולא הביא כפרתו קודם לתמיד, ואם לא יביאנה לא יאכל פסח, דמחוסר כפורים אסור בקדשים וענוש כרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:10:1.english: And one who lacks atonement - For example, a leper or a zav who forgot and did not bring his atonement [offering] before the daily [afternoon] offering; and if he does not bring it, he may not eat the Paschal [offering], for one who lacks atonement is forbidden [to partake] of sacrificial foods and is punished with karet [excision].

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:10:2.hebrew: שטובל - ואע"פ שטבל אתמול בשביעי שלו, צריך לטבול אחר שהביא כפרתו, דתנן בחומר בקודש (דף כא.): האונן והמחוסר כפורים צריכים טבילה לקודש:
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:10:2.english: That he immerses - Even though he immersed yesterday on his seventh [day], he must immerse after he has brought his atonement [offering], as we learned in [the chapter] Chomer BaKodesh ([Chagigah] 21a): An onen [acute mourner] and one who lacks atonement require immersion for consecrated [food].

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:11:1.hebrew: בשאר ימות השנה - אם הביא שלמי נדבה קודם התמיד והוא היה מחוסר כפורים, ואם לא יביא כפרתו לא יאכל את שלמיו, דכתיב "ואכלו אותם אשר כופר בהם". אלמא אכילת קדשים עשה היא, בין הנאכלים לכהנים בין הנאכלים לישראל:
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:11:1.english: On the rest of the days of the year - If he brought a voluntary peace-offering before the daily [afternoon] offering while he was lacking atonement, and if he does not bring his atonement [offering] he will not [be able to] eat his peace-offering, as it is written: "And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made." Thus, eating sacrificial food is a positive commandment, whether [sacrifices] eaten by priests or [those] eaten by Israelites.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:12:1.english: Of completion - "Upon it, complete [all the offerings]."

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:12:2.english: This positive commandment (of completion) than that positive commandment (of eating sacrificial meat):

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:13:1.hebrew: הכא - דקא"ר ישמעאל "אף מחוסר כפורים", במצורע עני קאמר, שמביא חטאת העוף ונאכלת לכהנים ואין בה הקטרה, ועשה דהשלמה גבי הקטרה כתיב. וטהרה של מחוסרי כפרה תלויה בחטאת, כדכתיב (ויקרא י״ב:ז׳) "והקריבו לפני ה' וכפר עלי'", ובחטאת קאי ביולדת:
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:13:1.english: Here - where Rabbi Yishmael said, "Even one lacking atonement," he is speaking of an impoverished leper, who brings a bird sin-offering, and it is eaten by the priests and has no burning [on the altar], and the positive commandment of completion is written regarding burning [on the altar]. And the purification of those lacking atonement depends on the sin-offering, as it is written (Leviticus 12:7): "And he shall offer it before the Lord, and make atonement for her," and [this verse] refers to the sin-offering, in [the passage of] a woman who has given birth.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:14:1.hebrew: מעלה ומלינה בראש המזבח - כדכתיב "והקריבו לפני ה' וכפר עליה", ולמחר יקטירנה לאחר תמיד של שחר. ולינה אינה פוסלת בראש המזבח, כדאמר בזבחים בפ' המזבח מקדש (זבחים דף פז.), לד"ה דלא ירדו:
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:14:1.english: He brings it up and leaves it overnight on the top of the altar - As it is written: "And he shall offer it before the Lord and atone for her," and on the morrow he burns it [on the altar] after the morning daily offering. And leaving [it] overnight does not disqualify [it] on the top of the altar, as it is stated in Zevachim in the chapter [entitled] Hamizbe'ach Mekadesh (Zevachim 87a), according to all opinions, that [once placed on the altar] they do not come down.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:15:1.english: But isn't there the guilt-offering of a leper - For [it] cannot be brought [as] a bird.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:16:1.hebrew: וכ"ת אשם לא מעכב - לא גר', דהיכי תיסק אדעתין דלא מעכב? הרי עיקר טהרה תלויה בו, שהרי נותן מדמו על גבי בהונות:
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:16:1.english: And if you say [that] a guilt-offering does not prevent [purification] - We do not read [this version], for how could it enter our mind that it does not prevent [purification]? Behold, the primary purification depends upon it, for [the priest] places [some] of its blood upon [the] thumbs and big toes.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:16:2.hebrew: בחטאת ואשם פשיטא לן דמעכבי טהרה לאכילת קדשים. חטאת — כדאשכחן ביולדת; אשם — שהרי ממנו לבהונות:
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:16:2.english: With regard to the sin-offering and guilt-offering, it is obvious to us that they prevent [his] purity for eating consecrated [foods]. The sin-offering — as we find regarding a woman who gave birth; the guilt-offering — for [some] of it [is applied] to the thumbs [and big toes].

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:17:1.hebrew: ואת השני - בתרי' דהאי קרא כתיב בשבועת ביטוי, וממילא ידעי' כיון דהאי שני עולה, חטאת הוה ראשון:
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:17:1.english: And the second - It is written after this verse, in [the passage of] an oath of utterance, and we automatically know [that] since this second [offering] is a burnt-offering, the sin-offering was first.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:18:1.hebrew: וקיימא לן - בזבחים בפרק כל התדיר (זבחים דף צ.), דהאי בנין אב לא איצטריך אלא לחטאת העוף הבאה עם עולת בהמה, כגון יולדת עשירה שמביאה עולתה בהמה וחטאתה עוף, שתקדים חטאת לעולה:
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:18:1.english: And we maintain - in Zevachim, in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaTadir (Zevachim 90a), that this paradigm is only needed for a bird sin-offering that comes with an animal burnt-offering, such as a wealthy woman who has given birth, who brings her burnt-offering [from] an animal and her sin-offering [from] a bird, that the sin-offering should precede the burnt-offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:18:2.english: This builds a prototype - Scripture built this structure [as] a prototype to teach regarding all sin-offerings that they should precede the burnt-offerings that come with them.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:1:1.hebrew: יאוחר דבר כו' - טעמא דרישא קא מפרש, תמיד קודם לפסח, דדין הוא שיאוחר הפסח — שנאמר בו ״בערב״ ו״בין הערבים״, ״תזבח את הפסח בערב״ (דברים ט״ז:ו׳), ״ושחטו אותו וגו'״ (שמות י״ב:ו׳) — לתמיד, שלא נאמר בו אלא ״את הכבש השני תעשה בין הערבים״ (במדבר כ״ח:ד׳):
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:1:1.english: An item should be deferred, etc. - [The Gemara] is explaining the reason for the first clause [of the Mishnah], that the daily offering precedes the Paschal lamb: for it is logical that the Paschal lamb — regarding which "in the evening" and "in the afternoon" are stated, "You shall sacrifice the Paschal lamb in the evening" (Deuteronomy 16:6) [and] "and ... shall slaughter it, etc." (Exodus 12:6) — should be deferred after the daily offering, regarding which only "The second lamb you shall offer in the afternoon" (Numbers 28:4) is stated.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:2:1.hebrew: אי הכי קטרת ונרות נמי ליקדמו לפסח - משום האי טעמא גופיה: יאוחר דבר כו'. דבקטרת ונרות חד "בין הערבים" כתיב: "ובהעלות אהרן את הנרות בין הערבים יקטירנה" (שמות ל׳:ח׳), ו"בין הערבים" אתרוייהו קאי:
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:2:1.english: If so, the incense and lamps should also precede the Paschal offering - Because of this very reason: "let the thing be postponed, etc." For regarding the incense and the lamps, [only] one "in the afternoon" is written: "And when Aaron lights the lamps in the afternoon, he shall burn it" (Exodus 30:8), and "in the afternoon" refers to both of them.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:3:1.english: As the Merciful One excluded - Regarding the lamps.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:3:2.hebrew: תן לה מדתה - חצי לוג לכל נר, דאין לך ליל ארוך שלא יהא לך בה כשיעור:
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:3:2.english: Give it its measure - Half a log [of oil] for each lamp, for there is no long night in which it would not have the [required] measure.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:4:1.english: It [is] from evening until morning, and no other [is] from evening until morning - And you have no service valid to begin after it.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:5:1.hebrew: ואתקש קטרת לנרות - מה נרות אין עבודה כשירה אחריה, אף קטרת אין עבודה כשירה אחריה:
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:5:1.english: And incense is juxtaposed to lamps - Just as [with] lamps, no service is valid after it, so too [with] incense, no service is valid after it.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:6:1.english: The daily offering precedes the incense, and the incense precedes the lamps - The reason is explained in Seder Yoma, in the chapter [entitled] Amar Lahen HaMemuneh.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:7:1.hebrew: ההוא למעוטי עבודה שבפנים - ההוא אותו לאו למעוטי פסח אתא, שהיא עבודת חוץ; דמסתברא דכי קא ממעיט, עבודת פנים דכוותה קממעיט — נרות עבודת פנים, וקטרת עבודת פנים:
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:7:1.english: That [word] is to exclude a service [performed] inside - That [word] "it" does not come to exclude the Paschal offering, which is an outside service; for it is reasonable that when [Scripture] excludes [something], it excludes an inside service like itself — [the] lamps are an inside service, and [the] incense is an inside service.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:8:1.english: The incense should be burning - It should already be burning.

Rashi on Pesachim 59a:8:2.hebrew: אין לך כל דבר באשים קודם לתמיד של שחר אלא קטורת, שנאמר בה בפרשת ואתה תצוה "בבקר בבקר", ובתמיד לא כתיב אלא חד "בקר":
Rashi on Pesachim 59a:8:2.english: You have nothing among the fire-offerings that precedes the morning daily burnt offering [tamid] except the incense, as it is stated regarding it in Parashat Ve'atah Tetzaveh: "in the morning, in the morning," whereas regarding the daily burnt offering only one "morning" is written.

Tosafot on Pesachim 59a:12:1.hebrew: אתי עשה דפסח דאית ביה כרת ודחי כו' - הקשה ריב"א: הא בעידנא דמיעקר עשה דהשלמה, לא מיקיים עשה דאכילת פסח, דאינה אלא בלילה! ותירץ: דמיירי שישחטו פסח עליו קודם שידחו עשה דהשלמה, דשוחטין וזורקין על טבול יום ומחוסר כפורים לכולי עלמא, אפילו לא יאכל לבסוף, הואיל ובידו תלוי, ופטור מפסח שני אפילו לא אכל; הלכך, כשהמקריב כפרתו מקיים עשה דפסח, דאז הוי ראוי לאכול, שאם לא היה יכול להקריב לא יהיה ראוי לאכול לערב, והפסח היה פסול. ור"י מתרץ: דדוקא בלא תעשה דחמיר בעינן בעידנא דמיעקר לאו דלקיים עשה, אבל עשה דחמיר דחי עשה הקל בכל ענין, אפילו לא מקיים עשה חמור בעידנא דקא עבר אעשה הקל, כדמוכח בהשולח (גיטין דף לח.) גבי רבי אליעזר ששיחרר עבדו, ובשילוח הקן (חולין דף קמא.) דהוה דחי עשה דמצורע דחמיר לעשה דשילוח הקן, אי לאו דאמר רחמנא "שלח תשלח" — אפי' לדבר מצוה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 59a:12:1.english: The positive commandment of the Paschal lamb, which carries karet, comes and overrides, etc. - Riva asked: Behold, at the time when the positive commandment of completion [of the daily sacrifices before the afternoon tamid] is uprooted, the positive commandment of eating the Paschal lamb is not fulfilled, for it [takes place] only at night! And he answered: [The Gemara] is speaking of a case where they slaughter the Paschal lamb for him before they override the positive commandment of completion — for according to all opinions, one may slaughter [the Paschal lamb] and sprinkle [its blood] on behalf of a tevul yom or one who lacks atonement, even if he will not eat [it] in the end, since it is within his power [to become fit], and he is exempt from the Second Passover even if he did not eat [it]. Therefore, when he offers his atonement [sacrifice], he fulfills the positive commandment of the Paschal lamb, for then he becomes fit to eat [it]; whereas if he were not able to offer [it], he would not be fit to eat in the evening, and the Paschal lamb would be invalid. And Ri answers: Specifically regarding a negative commandment, which is stringent, do we require that at the time the prohibition is uprooted, the positive commandment be fulfilled; however, a stringent positive commandment overrides a lenient positive commandment in any case, even if he does not fulfill the stringent positive commandment at the time he transgresses the lenient positive commandment, as is proven in [the chapter] HaSholeach (Gittin 38a) regarding Rabbi Eliezer who freed his slave, and in [the chapter] Shiluach HaKen (Chullin 141a), where the stringent positive commandment of a metzora would have overridden the positive commandment of sending away [the mother bird from] the nest, were it not that the Merciful One stated, "You shall surely send away" — [meaning] even for a mitzvah matter.

Tosafot on Pesachim 59a:18:1.hebrew: זה בנה אב לכל חטאות כו' - ואפילו לעכב קאמר, דאי למצוה, אכתי לימא "בשקרבה". הקשה ריב"א, דבת"כ (תזריע יולדת פרק ד מ"ג) משמע דליכא עיכובא, דקתני התם גבי יולדת: שאם הביאה עולתה, תביא חטאתה ממין עולתה. ובפרק כל התדיר (זבחים דף צ.) משמע דלא אצטריך האי "זה בנה אב" אלא לחטאת העוף הבאה עם עולת בהמה, וליכא כי אם יולדת עשירה; ובמסכת קנים (פ"ב) נמי אמרינן: "האשה שהביאה חטאתה ומתה, מביאין יורשים עולתה" כו', "עולתה ומתה, לא יביאו יורשים חטאתה" — משמע קצת: אם היתה קיימת, לא היתה מביאה אלא חטאתה. ותירץ רבינו חיים כהן: דהא דפריך הכא "ואפילו עיכובא יהא", היינו דוקא במצורע, דכתיב ביה "תהיה" דמשמע עיכובא, כדאמר בריש הקומץ רבה (מנחות דף יט.); ומשני דכתיב "והעלה", למעוטי מעיכובא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 59a:18:1.english: "This is a paradigm for all sin-offerings, etc." - And [the Gemara] is saying [that the sin-offering must precede the burnt-offering] even as an indispensable requirement, for if [it were only] a mitzvah [to offer it first], still let [the Gemara] answer "when [his burnt-offering] was already offered." Riva raised a difficulty: for in Torat Kohanim (Tazria, Yoledet, Chapter 4, Mishnah 3) it is implied that there is no indispensability, as it teaches there regarding a woman who gave birth that if she brought her burnt-offering [first], she brings her sin-offering from the species of her burnt-offering. And in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaTadir (Zevachim 90a), it is implied that this [principle of] "this is a paradigm" is needed only for a bird sin-offering that comes with an animal burnt-offering, and there is no [such case] except a wealthy woman who gave birth; and in Tractate Kinnim (Chapter 2) we also say: "A woman who brought her sin-offering and died — [her] heirs bring her burnt-offering, etc.; [if she brought] her burnt-offering and died — [her] heirs do not bring her sin-offering" — implying somewhat [that] if she were alive, she would bring only her sin-offering. And Rabbeinu Chaim Kohen resolved [this]: that what [the Gemara] asks here — "even [if] there should be indispensability" — that is specifically regarding a metzora, concerning whom it is written "tihyeh" ("shall be"), which implies indispensability, as [the Gemara] says at the beginning of HaKometz Rabbah (Menachot 19a); and [the Gemara] answers that it is written "vehe'elah" ("and he shall offer"), to exclude [it] from indispensability.

Tosafot on Pesachim 59a:19:1.hebrew: דכתיב והעלה - ודוקא בדיעבד, דהא כתיב בהדיא: "ואחר ישחט את העולה":
Tosafot on Pesachim 59a:19:1.english: As it is written: "And [the priest] shall offer" - And [this is] specifically after the fact [bedi'avad], for it is explicitly written: "and afterward he shall slaughter the burnt-offering":

Tosafot on Pesachim 59a:1:1.hebrew: יאוחר דבר כו' - אע"ג דתמיד תדיר, איצטריך למיכתב דה"א שהפסח יקדים משום "עליה השלם":
Tosafot on Pesachim 59a:1:1.english: An item should be delayed, etc. - Even though the daily offering is more frequent, it was [still] necessary to write [the verses teaching this], because one might have thought that the Paschal offering should precede [the daily offering] because of [the principle], "upon it, complete [all the offerings]."

Tosafot on Pesachim 59a:6:1.hebrew: קטרת ונרות נקדמו לפסח - הקשה ריב"א: והלא בנרות כתיב נמי "מערב ועד בקר", ומה לי "מערב" ומה לי "בערב"? ויש לומר ד"מערב ועד בקר" איצטריך ליתן לה מדתה, ולא לאיחור:
Tosafot on Pesachim 59a:6:1.english: Incense and lamps should precede the Paschal lamb - Riva raised a difficulty: Is it not also written regarding the lamps, "from evening until morning," and what is the difference between "from evening" and "in the evening"? And one can answer that "from evening until morning" is needed to give it its measure [of oil], and not to delay [it].

Tosafot on Pesachim 59a:9:1.hebrew: אין לך דבר שמתעכב כו' אלא קטרת - נראה לר"י דלא גרס "ונרות", דע"כ לא חשיב אלא מידי דהקטרה, דבה הקפידה תורה לאחר, כדכתיב: "והקטיר עליה חלבי" וגו'. דאי לא תימא הכי, ליחשוב נמי ברישא: "אין לך שקודם לתמיד של שחר אלא קטרת, ודישון מזבח הפנימי, ושני גזרי עצים, והטבת נרות", דקודמין לתמיד כל הני, כדאמרינן באמר להן הממונה (יומא דף לג). ובתוספתא נמי ליתא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 59a:9:1.english: "Nothing may be delayed, etc., except the incense" - It appears to the Ri that [the text] does not read "and the lamps," for perforce [the baraita] only counts items involving burning [on the altar], regarding which the Torah was particular to place last, as it is written: "And he shall burn upon it the fats [of the peace-offerings]," etc. [Leviticus 6:5]. For if you do not say so, let it also count in the first clause: "Nothing precedes the daily morning offering except the incense, the clearing of the ashes from the inner altar, the two logs of wood, and the dressing of the lamps," for all of these precede the daily offering, as we say in [the chapter] Amar Lahem HaMemuneh (Yoma 33). And in the Tosefta as well, [the phrase "and the lamps"] is not [found].
